# Class 10 biology, ~2 minutes, written by Claude for F-014 S3 (processes). Expect: a content slide on the heart; "let
# me show you how the human heart pumps blood" opens simulation mode (four chambers, the six steps drawn, unnamed);
# the heart rate (72 beats per minute) and the stroke volume (70 mL per beat) print, with T = 0.833 s and cardiac
# output 5.04 L/min computed; each step said moves the stage (right atrium ... aorta); "the heart of the matter" is a
# trap; "let's get back to the slides" ends the mode with a recap; then the slides go on (blood vessels).
@setup subject=Biology grade=10 topic="The human heart"

Good morning class. Today we will study the human heart and how it pumps blood.
[pause 1]
The heart is a muscular organ about the size of your fist. It has four chambers: two atria on top and two ventricles below.
The right side carries deoxygenated blood and the left side carries oxygenated blood. This is called double circulation.
[pause 1.5]
Let me show you how the human heart pumps blood.
A normal heart beats about 72 times a minute, and each beat pumps out about 70 mL of blood.
[pause 1]
Deoxygenated blood from the body enters the right atrium through the vena cava.
The right atrium contracts and pushes the blood into the right ventricle through the tricuspid valve.
The right ventricle then pumps it to the lungs through the pulmonary artery.
[pause 1]
In the lungs the blood picks up oxygen. Oxygenated blood returns to the left atrium through the pulmonary veins.
From the left atrium the blood passes into the left ventricle through the mitral valve.
The left ventricle has the thickest wall, because it pumps oxygenated blood to the rest of the body through the aorta.
[pause 1.5]
And that is really the heart of the matter: the valves make sure blood flows only one way.
[pause 1]
Okay, let's get back to the slides.
[pause 1]
Blood vessels are of three types: arteries, veins and capillaries.
Arteries carry blood away from the heart, and veins bring it back to the heart.
